questions.question: Use calculate_correlation with method equal to pearson and use identify_clusters with n_clusters equal to 3, method equal to kmeans and use zoom_2d_region with x_range from 10.0 to 30.0, y_range from 10000.0 to 20000.0 in order to know What patterns can be observed in the relationship between commute distance, income levels, and employee retention across different departments?

answer.value: The scatter plot reveals several key patterns: Engineering and IT departments show higher income clusters ($10K-$21K) with moderate attrition rates around 9%. HR department has lower average income ($7K) but also lower attrition (7.3%). Distance from home shows minimal correlation with income across all departments, averaging around 10 miles. Employees with attrition tend to have slightly lower average income ($8,314 vs $9,033). Work-life balance scores are evenly distributed across income levels, suggesting it is not a primary income determinant.

key_insights: Engineering and IT have highest income levels
Distance from home has weak correlation with income
Attrition is slightly higher among lower income employees
